description: Per-delivery re-signing for the v0.5 entry kinds (§9.8, inheriting §9.7): an entry may rest in a mailbox arbitrarily long, so the Hub MUST re-sign EVERY delivery (first delivery, visibility-timeout redelivery, stream push) with a fresh `t`/`jti` — only t/jti change between deliveries; the bound context is otherwise identical. This fixture pins TWO deliveries of the dp-011 message entry: same entry, same payload_sha256, two (t, jti) pairs, two distinct pinned signatures — each verifying against its own header, proving freshness is achievable without altering the bound content.
obligation: Reproduce BOTH pinned `v1` values (each over the base context + its delivery's t/jti). Hub-side: every delivery of an entry MUST carry a fresh t/jti — replaying an earlier delivery's header verbatim is non-conformant. Consumer-side: reject a `t` outside the +/-replay window (an old delivery's header naturally ages out) and a replayed `jti` within the cache TTL (>= window) — a redelivered entry is NOT a replay (its header is fresh); the same jti presented twice IS. Expected runner wiring (#26): sign the base context once per delivery entry (t/jti substituted) and compare each v1.
